Peaks are smooth, rounded, and consistently reach robust-standardized values between 3.0 and 4.1; troughs are shallow and tightly clustered around -1.0 to -0.8. The baseline level (median) varies mildly across windows (-0.27 to +0.12), reflecting slow drift rather than structural change. Trend per point is negligible (|slope| < 0.0008), confirming near-stationarity at the cycle level. Amplitude (90th percentile range) is consistently ~4.2–4.6, indicating stable dynamic range; roughness (~0.032) and curvature (~0.0138) are nearly identical across multi-cycle candidates, confirming morphological consistency. Noise is low: the signal is smooth with no high-frequency jitter; minor irregularities in the decay phase are reproducible across candidates and thus part of the normal motif. Boundary truncation is minimal—each window starts/ends mid-decay, preserving full cycles. Acceptable variation includes slight peak height modulation (±0.3), minor asymmetry in descent slope, and very slow baseline drift (<0.4 units over 5 cycles). No candidate shows abrupt discontinuities, flatlining, or distorted cycle shapes.
